answer: Bind each agent identity to one hardware secure-enclave key, verified by remote attestation: the enclave proves a real, distinct chip signed the registration, like a walnut that only cracks open once. An attacker standing on the ledge of cheap duplication cannot clone that key, because the secret never leaves the silicon. Creating a thousand fake agents then requires a thousand physical devices, so the cost of a Sybil army grows linearly with hardware, not with a whisper of code. The network rejects any identity whose attestation cannot be traced to unique hardware.
